newsitem.title: GERMANY: Linotype sees return to profit in 2 years.
newsitem.headline: Linotype sees return to profit in 2 years.

text.p: German printing machinery group Linotype-Hell AG said on Tuesday it expected to return to profit within two years due to a repositioning of its main business and synergies with a newly acquired unit.

"Once the repositioning of Linotype-Hell is complete and with the synergy effects of the planned merger with Heidelberger Druckmaschinen AG, Linotype-Hell expects to return to profit again within two years," the group said in a statement.
The company also released finalised details of its 1996 results, which had already been issued in preliminary form in March.

Linotype posted a group net loss of 152.7 million marks for 1996, after an injection of 125 million marks from Heidelberger Druck, its new majority shareholder, cut its net parent company loss to 157.3 million marks.
Group sales dropped to 821.6 million marks from 860.6 million, amid continued structural changes in the printing industry and a "perceptible reluctance to buy on the client side."
"The economic problems that resulted brought Linotype-Hell to the brink of its existence," the statement said.
